issues.detail: The Vietnamese 'con' (child/offspring) is added or substituted for 'αρσεν' (male/man). The Greek specifically specifies 'every male', not just any child.

The Vietnamese omits the word 'hành động' or equivalent for 'διανοιγον' (opening/breaking), but more importantly, it fails to capture that the 'opening of the womb' is the condition/action leading to the naming. The phrase 'mở dạ con' is slightly ambiguous compared to the Greek 'αρσεν διανοιγον μητραν' (male opening [of] the womb).
